metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness persists each pending provider retry, but the DSH adapter skips llm/retry records and cannot paint the required retry window red; the shared OpenAI error mock now makes the cell recordable.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The scenario requires one stable session to follow ready -> working -> error -> ready. The session must enter error when the first provider retry is scheduled. It must stay in error across later attempts. It must never enter waiting. It must return to ready only after a successful turn/end.

## Agent support

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 implements this behavior explicitly. The installed dsh-base composition mounts dsh-llm-retry. The installed retry package documents a default normal policy with five retries for RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT, and EMPTY_RESPONSE. Its implementation appends a durable llm/retry record before each backoff and a durable llm/retry-started record before the next attempt. The pi-ai adapter maps messages that contain a 5xx status to SERVER. Therefore, HTTP 529 is eligible.

The committed DeepSeek Harness 2-14 transcript also measures this behavior. The transcript contains five llm/retry records and five llm/retry-started records with increasing delays before the final failed turn/end. The failure is TRANSPORT rather than HTTP 529. However, the recording proves that the installed agent loop writes the documented durable retry records on the exact TUI profile that this recipe drives.

## Daemon capability

The DSH adapter mishandles the available trace. core/adapters/inbound/agents/dsh/parser.go declares handlers for session, turn, approval, message, tool, and request records only. ParseLine sets Skip=true for each unknown type. Therefore, the parser discards llm/retry and llm/retry-started.

The committed 2-14 recording gives concrete daemon evidence. Its transcript records retry scheduling from sequence 16 through sequence 29. Its events.jsonl enters working at sequence 255. It does not enter error during the retry ladder. It enters error at sequence 420 only after the terminal error turn/end. Thus, the daemon does not paint a pending retry red although the source contains the required signal.

This result is a bug, not an architectural limit. tailer.SessionError already has ErrorPhaseRetrying, Attempt, MaxAttempts, RetryIn, Class, and Message. A successful turn_done already clears a retrying error. The DSH parser must map llm/retry to that existing shape. The spec remains known-failing and asserts the correct arc.

## Driver capability and recording fixture

The recipe uses send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean. The DeepSeek Harness interactive driver declares and implements all four steps. The driver also accepts model, base_url, context_window, permission_mode, and api_key settings. It writes those settings into a temporary OpenAI-compatible provider patch. Therefore, the script driver is ready.

Commit 61cda4ff3 supplies the shared tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-error package. Its route is POST /v1/chat/completions, which matches the driver's openai-completions provider and the configured /v1 base URL. With --status 529, --error-type overloaded_error, and --succeed-after 3, it fails three counted primary requests and streams a successful fourth response with non-zero usage. Its case-insensitive title filter matches the installed dsh-session-title-llm system prompt, "Create a concise title for an AI coding-assistant session...". Matching title requests return success and stay at counter #0.

The package tests passed with the race detector. An exact local protocol probe also returned 200 for the title request, 529 for primary requests #1 through #3, and 200 plus a valid SSE completion for primary request #4. The request-log pattern excludes title line #0 and matches only counted primary lines. Thus, title traffic cannot consume a retry slot or satisfy the mock-use guard.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: the cell would pass without proving provider retry if the mock served the main request successfully on its first attempt or if a session-title request consumed the configured failure slots. The transcript spec therefore requires exactly three llm/retry records with failure.code SERVER. The request-log pattern counts only primary request lines #1 and later, not title line #0.

Load-bearing mock contract: tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-error must serve POST /v1/chat/completions, fail the first three counted primary requests with HTTP 529 overloaded_error, and stream a successful fourth response with non-zero usage. Its case-insensitive title filter must keep the installed DSH title prompt at counter #0.

The committed measured retry fixture uses TRANSPORT failures, not HTTP 529. The installed pi-ai adapter source maps 5xx error text to SERVER, and the installed retry policy includes SERVER. A live recording must confirm that the mock produces that durable failure code.

The model observation remains intentionally unpinned until the live recording confirms which DSH source label reaches the websocket. The driver configures qwen/qwen3.5-9b, while the mock response carries mock-openai-error-model.
The llm/retry record means that another attempt is scheduled. It does not prove recovery. The transcript assertions separately require one completed turn/end and forbid an error turn/end.
The five-second post-turn sleep matches the longest committed sibling delay. It gives irrlichd time to publish the recovered ready state before exit_clean removes the live process.

Load-bearing isolation precondition: the driver must keep its fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker, and run-cell.sh must verify that the mock served counted primary requests. Otherwise, another DSH transcript or the real provider could satisfy the lifecycle phases.

sources.note: Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 package contract: default normal mode retries RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT, and EMPTY_RESPONSE up to five times, and each scheduled attempt reaches the durable session log before backoff.
The shipped backoff function appends llm/retry before its cancellable delay and llm/retry-started before returning retry to the agent loop.
The shipped pi-ai adapter classifies error text containing 429 or rate-limit as RATE_LIMIT and text containing any 5xx status as SERVER. Both codes are retryable under the default policy.
Measured DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 trace: lines 18-31 contain five durable llm/retry and llm/retry-started pairs with retry numbers 1-5 and increasing delayMs values before the terminal failed boundary.
Concrete daemon result for the measured retry trace: ready->working at sequence 255, no error during the five scheduled retries, then working->error only at sequence 420 after terminal turn_done.
recordHandlers has no llm/retry or llm/retry-started entry. ParseLine marks every unrecognized record Skip=true. parseTurnEnd handles only the eventual completed or terminal boundary.
SessionError already represents retrying failures with attempt, maximum-attempt, retry-delay, class, and message fields; ClearedByTurnBoundary clears ErrorPhaseRetrying on the eventual turn_done.
ErrorPhaseRetrying is the domain shape for holding a session red for the whole retry window rather than flickering per attempt.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean. It applies the recipe model, base URL, context window, permission mode, and API key through a temporary provider patch.

Commit 61cda4ff3 supplies the shared POST /v1/chat/completions mock. It supports fail-N-then-recover behavior, SSE success with usage, a case-insensitive ignored-request filter, and distinct #0 versus counted request logs.

go test ./tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-error/... -race -count=1 passed. The tests cover failure then recovery and prove that title requests return success without incrementing the primary counter.
The installed 0.1.5-rc.2 title package starts its stable system prompt with Create a concise title for an AI coding-assistant session, which matches the mock's case-insensitive filter.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the community TUI profile is installed under ~/.dsh/profiles/tui
port 18805 is free on 127.0.0.1 at record time
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: run-cell.sh builds and launches tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-error on 127.0.0.1:18805 before the driver starts

the mock ignores the DSH title-generation request for failure counting, fails the first three counted primary POST /v1/chat/completions requests with HTTP 529 overloaded_error, and succeeds on the fourth with an ok completion and non-zero usage

the interactive driver creates a fresh cwd and pre-launch marker, exports the configured non-empty API key through LMSTUDIO_API_KEY, applies a temporary OpenAI-compatible provider patch with base URL http://127.0.0.1:18805/v1, and launches dsh --profile tui in tmux
the driver resolves only the post-marker compressed transcript whose session header has the fresh cwd

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: the same DSH session follows ready -> working -> error -> ready and never enters waiting
the durable transcript contains exactly three llm/retry records with failure.code SERVER before one completed turn/end
the session enters error once and stays there across the complete retry window
the completed turn clears the retrying error and leaves the session ready before exit_clean
the mock log contains four counted primary request lines (#1 through #4); title traffic is logged as #0 and does not consume the failure counter
the live observation vector reports non-zero tokens and zero known cost; record fills the exact model from the recording
recipe.scope_note: Uses the muse sibling's five-second post-turn sleep, the longest committed sibling delay. The claudecode sibling has no sleep, but DSH writes compressed frames and the hold keeps recovery observable before exit_clean. The 180-second timeout matches both committed sibling recipes and exceeds the default three-retry backoff window by a wide margin.
